scope.scopeNotesMd: This report analyzes the base `Reference` datatype StructureDefinition in R4 and R6 ballot4, including its local child elements (`reference`, `type`, `identifier`, `display`), local invariants (`ref-1`, `ref-2`), flags, bindings, and the directly bound `resource-types` terminology. Changes inherited only from `Element`, `DataType`, `Extension`, or global datatype hierarchy remodeling are excluded from `findings[]` per the assignment rule.
outOfScope: The R4-to-R6 baseDefinition shift from `Element` to `DataType` for datatypes, including class hierarchy and generated superclass impacts, is treated as an inherited/base-artifact concern rather than a local Reference finding.
Changes to inherited `Reference.id` and `Reference.extension` content, slicing, or base constraints are delegated to Element/DataType/Extension analyses.

Reference target restrictions on resource-specific elements such as `Observation.subject` or `MedicationRequest.requester` are outside this datatype report; those belong to the owning resource element reports.
The addition, removal, or renaming of FHIR resources themselves is not reported as a resource-level finding here, except for its local impact on the `Reference.type` binding.
Search parameters, operations, profiles, implementation guides, and server CapabilityStatement behavior are outside this Reference datatype scope.

narrativeReportMd:
# Reference R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Reference` keeps the same canonical identity and the same local element set, cardinalities, JSON property names, primitive/datatype choices, modifier flags, and summary flags. One direct local hard break was found: R6 adds invariant `ref-2`, so an R4-valid Reference that only carries `type` is no longer valid unless it also has `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, or an extension.

## Scope
The analysis is scoped to the base `Reference` datatype. Inherited `Element`/`DataType` hierarchy changes are explicitly out of scope, even though R6 changes the baseDefinition from `Element` to `DataType`.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is validation-oriented rather than structural: check for type-only references, update cross-version handling for the changed local-reference invariant, and review `Reference.type` resource-type code handling because the bound value set now represents the R6 resource universe.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest impact finding is `Reference:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Reference:ref2-added:5e0c9a`, the new `ref-2` invariant. The terminology finding `Reference:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Reference.type:2d4b71` is also important for converters and generated enums because many R4 resource-type codes disappear from the R6 value set and R6 adds new codes not known to R4.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for resource-type code migration. The package definitions identify added and removed codes, but they do not provide authoritative ConceptMaps for renamed or retired resources.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The new `ref-2` rule appears justified because `Reference.type` describes the expected target type but does not identify a target. A less-breaking alternative would have been a warning or transitional invariant, but that would preserve ambiguous type-only references.

## Follow-up analysis
The global datatype base hierarchy should be owned by the `DataType`/`Element` reports. Resource additions/removals and resource-specific reference target changes should be handled by the reports for those resources and elements.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: One local hard validation break was found: R6 forbids `Reference` instances that only specify `type`. Additional migration risks are the changed local-reference invariant for `reference="#"` and the version-specific resource-type code set used by `Reference.type`. The main uncertainty is not the computable diff, but the absence of official rationale and ConceptMaps for resource-type code migration.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should scan all Reference-valued elements for objects that contain `type` without `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, or `extension`; these need either a resolvable/logical target, display text, an extension, or removal if they were placeholders. Cross-version converters should also treat `reference="#"` as R6-only unless they can prove the R4 target context permits an equivalent representation. Code generators and validators should regenerate resource-type enums from the target FHIR version rather than assuming the R4 and R6 `resource-types` value sets are interchangeable.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition differences because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present and directly comparable. Confidence is medium for the real-world migration severity of `Reference.type` terminology because the packages show code-set changes but do not provide official resource rename/removal mappings or a terminology-server expansion trace.

findings.title: R6 adds ref-2, disallowing Reference instances that only carry type

oldState.summary: R4 had no local invariant requiring one of reference, identifier, display, or extension.

constraints.human: SHALL have a contained resource if a local reference is provided

semanticText.definition: A reference from one resource to another.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the local Reference constraints did not say that a Reference must contain a target-identifying field. A Reference object containing only `type` could satisfy the inherited element-content rule because `type` is a child element.

newState.summary: R6 adds ref-2 requiring reference, identifier, display, or extension.

constraints.human: At least one of reference, identifier and display SHALL be present (unless an extension is provided).
constraints.expression: reference.exists() or identifier.exists() or display.exists() or extension.exists()

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires a Reference to include `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, or an extension. The `type` element is intentionally not sufficient because it constrains the expected target type but does not identify a target.

facts.newValue: reference.exists() or identifier.exists() or display.exists() or extension.exists()

facts.oldValue: type-only Reference was not locally prohibited
facts.newValue: type is not one of the fields satisfying ref-2

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break for Reference fragments that contain `type` but lack `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, and extensions. Runtime risk is medium because generated validators, schemas, and custom business rules may now reject placeholder references that older systems accepted. It does not create a meaningful R6-to-R4 representability problem because R4 can carry the fields R6 requires.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The affected pattern is usually a placeholder or weakly specified reference rather than a resolvable clinical link, but rejection during migration can still interrupt workflows or expose missing target data.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure that a Reference actually identifies or describes a target instead of only naming an expected target type.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep type-only Reference instances valid in the base datatype and express ref-2 first as a warning, best-practice invariant, or profile-level rule.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `Reference.type` constrains an expected target type but does not identify or describe a target. Making `ref-2` an error creates a real R4-to-R6 validation break for type-only placeholders, but the less-breaking warning/profile alternative leaves those ambiguous references valid in the base model. Because that tradeoff is material, the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained the R4-valid shape and added a warning-level invariant or profile guidance requiring `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, or an extension. That would protect existing type-only instances during transition, but it would only partially meet the R6 goal because conformant base instances could still contain no target-identifying information.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old placeholder data, but it would not give base R6 the stronger guarantee that a Reference carries target-identifying content.

evidence.detail: R4 Reference root has `ref-1` but no `ref-2` invariant.
R6 Reference root adds `ref-2` as an error-level invariant.
evidence.quote: reference.exists() or identifier.exists() or display.exists() or extension.exists()

evidence.detail: R6 records `ref-2` as a condition on the target-identifying children, reinforcing that these elements participate in the invariant.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are Reference fragments. The R4 fragment with only `type` is the affected pattern; the migration example is only valid if the target reference can actually be determined.

findings.narrativeMd: `Reference.type` names the expected target type, but it is not a reference target. R6 makes that distinction enforceable with `ref-2`: existing R4 data that used `{ "type": "Patient" }` as a placeholder Reference must now provide an actual literal reference, logical identifier, display text, or extension. This is hard breaking for strict validation because the JSON shape can be syntactically unchanged while the invariant result changes from pass to fail.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid Reference with only `type` can become R6-invalid. The break is local to the datatype invariant and will surface through R6 validators, generated model validation, profile validators that inherit base constraints, and any FHIRPath-based quality checks. R6-valid References remain representable in R4 for this change because R4 already supports `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, and extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan Reference-valued elements for objects where `type.exists()` is true but `reference`, `identifier`, `display`, and `extension` are all absent. If the target can be resolved, populate `reference`; if only a business identifier is known, populate `identifier`; if only human-readable context is known, consider `display`; if the content is genuinely extension-only, carry it as a governed extension. Do not fabricate a literal reference from `type` alone without source data.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably avoidable as an immediate hard error by first introducing a warning-level or best-practice rule. However, a type-only Reference is not operationally useful as a reference, so the stricter base rule is defensible. The tradeoff is between cleaner R6 semantics and migration friction for historical placeholder data.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds an error-level ref-2 invariant requiring a Reference to contain reference, identifier, display, or extension. That makes an R4-valid type-only placeholder such as a Reference carrying only type fail R6 validation, so this is a real old-valid/new-invalid break. The break is on a normative core datatype, which matters, but type alone does not identify a target or provide useful display/identifier semantics. Requiring at least one actionable target-bearing or explanatory child is proportionate even though historical placeholder data may need cleanup.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-Reference snapshot Reference.constraint has ref-1 and ele-1 but no ref-2.
R6 StructureDefinition-Reference snapshot Reference.constraint adds ref-2 with severity error and expression: reference.exists() or identifier.exists() or display.exists() or extension.exists().
R6 marks ref-2 as a condition on Reference.reference, Reference.identifier, and Reference.display; Reference.type does not satisfy it.
R4 Reference is marked normative with normativeVersion 4.0.0 in the StructureDefinition/maturity inputs.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative R4 status raises the compatibility burden for a new hard invariant. It did not change the judgment to Revisit because the invalidated pattern is a targetless Reference rather than a semantically complete reference.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a Reference with only type, or otherwise lacking reference, identifier, display, and extension, can pass R4 base constraints but fail R6 ref-2 as an error invariant.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level or best-practice invariant would be less breaking, and a transition period would reduce migration friction. Counting type as satisfying the rule would preserve more R4 data but would defeat the R6 goal because type is only an expected target class, not a reference target. The plausible less-breaking designs therefore carry meaningful semantic and conformance tradeoffs.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies a hard R4-to-R6 validation break and medium migration risk. I agree that the break is defensible, but I treat the warning-level alternative as only partially less-breaking because it would not meet the same enforcement goal.

findings.title: R6 ref-1 allows reference="#" in contained-resource context

oldState.summary: R4 ref-1 allowed non-local references or local fragment references matching a contained resource id.

constraints.human: SHALL have a contained resource if a local reference is provided

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 invariant did not include a special case for a bare `#` reference. A local reference had to either not start with `#` or resolve the fragment after `#` to a contained resource id.

newState.summary: R6 ref-1 wraps the test in reference.exists() and adds a special case for reference="#" when rootResource differs from resource.

constraints.human: SHALL have a contained resource if a local reference is provided
constraints.expression: reference.exists()  implies (reference.startsWith('#').not() or (reference.substring(1).trace('url') in %rootResource.contained.id.trace('ids')) or (reference='#' and %rootResource!=%resource))

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the ordinary contained-resource id check but explicitly permits a bare `#` reference when the reference is being evaluated from a contained resource rather than from the root resource.

facts.newValue: reference.exists()  implies (reference.startsWith('#').not() or (reference.substring(1).trace('url') in %rootResource.contained.id.trace('ids')) or (reference='#' and %rootResource!=%resource))

facts.oldValue: R4 rejected the bare fragment form under ref-1
facts.newValue: R6 can accept the bare fragment form in contained-resource context

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is primarily a loosening for R4-to-R6 and a narrow R6-to-R4 round-trip risk. R6 content that uses `reference="#"` from a contained resource context may fail R4 validation because R4 lacks the special case. The pattern is context-sensitive and likely rare, so runtime impact is low.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If mishandled, a converter might lose or reject a back-reference from contained content to its containing resource, but the affected form is specialized.

justification.inferredGoal: Support a contained resource referring to its containing/root resource using the bare local reference form.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is a narrow R6 loosening and R6-to-R4 down-conversion concern, not an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The changed `ref-1` expression adds a context-limited allowance for `reference="#"` only when `%rootResource != %resource`. That does not invalidate R4 content when moving to R6; it expands what R6 can express. The remaining compatibility cost is that some R6-valid content may not validate as R4, so a backward-compatible alternative judgment is not applicable under the R4-to-R6 calibration rule.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed because R4-valid references are not made invalid by this change. A design that simply avoided the new bare-`#` form would be a conservative cross-version authoring rule, not a backwards-compatible alternative to a breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoiding bare `#` would improve down-conversion compatibility but would withhold the R6-contained-resource reference semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 ref-1 has no `reference='#'` special case.
R6 ref-1 adds the bare `#` special case and guards evaluation with `reference.exists() implies`.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative and is R6-valid only in the contained-resource context where `%rootResource != %resource`; the same literal fragment at the root resource level is not made generally valid by this invariant.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes `ref-1` from a simple local-fragment containment check into a context-sensitive rule. The newly allowed `reference="#"` form matters for reverse/context references involving contained resources. It is not an R4-to-R6 break; instead, it creates a small risk that valid R6 content cannot be validated or faithfully represented as R4 without avoiding or transforming that reference form.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators evaluating the R4 `ref-1` expression can reject a bare `#` local reference because there is no fragment id after the hash to match against `contained.id`. R6 validators can accept it only when `%rootResource != %resource`. Strict cross-version validators and converters therefore need context-aware handling rather than a simple string-level rule.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4 conversion, detect `Reference.reference` equal to `#`. If the reference occurs in a contained-resource context, either retain it with an explicit compatibility warning, map it using an implementation-specific extension, or avoid down-conversion when the relationship is semantically important. Add tests for root-resource and contained-resource contexts because the same string has different validity.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 change appears narrowly justified to express a relationship R4 did not model cleanly. A more R4-compatible design would have avoided the new bare-`#` form, but that would require another representation or leave the intended contained-to-root reference ambiguous.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The ref-1 change is not an R4-to-R6 breaking constraint. R6 wraps the check in reference.exists() implies and adds a narrow contained-resource special case for reference="#" when the root resource is not the current resource. Existing R4-valid references remain acceptable; the only compatibility issue is reverse-direction handling for new R6 content that uses the bare hash form.
keyEvidence: R4 ref-1 expression requires non-hash references or a fragment id matching a contained resource id.
R6 ref-1 expression adds reference.exists() implies and the special case reference='#' and %rootResource!=%resource.
The existing report also characterizes the affected direction as R6-to-R4 with low risk.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative R4 status would matter for a direct R4-to-R6 break, but this change is a narrowing of R4 validation risk only in the reverse direction, so maturity does not create a concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break; only R6 instances using the new bare '#' contained-resource form may not validate or round-trip cleanly as R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed because R4 consumers are not broken. Avoiding the new bare '#' form would be more R4-compatible for down-conversion, but it would also forgo the R6 representation that the special case was added to support.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing low-impact, reverse-direction assessment matches the fresh review; this is not a hard R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: Reference.type still binds to resource-types, but the R6 resource-type code set is substantially different

oldState.summary: R4 Reference.type is a uri with an extensible binding to ValueSet/resource-types version 4.0.1.

binding.description: Aa resource (or, for logical models, the URI of the logical model).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The comparison used the R4 complete CodeSystem/resource-types and the R6 ValueSet/resource-types compose concepts, not a live terminology-server expansion.

semanticText.definition: The expected type of the target of the reference.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 bound `Reference.type` to the versioned R4 set of resource type names. The binding was extensible, but R4 validators and generated enums commonly use this value set as the known resource-type universe.

newState.summary: R6 Reference.type remains uri 0..1 with extensible binding to the same ValueSet canonical, but the value set content and included system change to the R6 fhir-types resource list.

binding.description: Aa resource (or, for logical models, the URI of the logical model).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 ValueSet/resource-types explicitly includes 127 concrete resource type concepts from `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types`; R4's resource-types code system contained 148 concepts.

semanticText.short: Type the reference refers to (e.g. "Patient") - must be a resource in resources
semanticText.definition: The expected type of the target of the reference.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the same element shape but changes the versioned code universe. Some R4 type strings are no longer R6 resource types, and R6 introduces type strings that R4 does not know.

facts.note: Canonical value set URL did not change.
Codes present in the R4 resource-types code system but not in the R6 ValueSet/resource-types compose.
Codes present in the R6 ValueSet/resource-types compose but not in the R4 resource-types code system.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Reference.type` matches by identical element id and path. The terminology comparison is between the versioned packages' `ValueSet/resource-types` definitions and their referenced/embedded code lists.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `Reference.type` is still a `uri` and the binding remains extensible, so the base datatype does not create a simple required-binding hard error. However, many implementations generate resource-type enums, switch statements, validation warnings/errors, and resolver logic from this value set. R4 instances using removed resource-type strings can become non-conformant or fail stricter R6 tooling; R6 instances using new resource-type strings cannot be cleanly represented as R4 resource-type values.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect resource-type handling can misroute reference resolution or cause data loss during down-conversion, especially when the referenced target resource itself has no R4 counterpart.

justification.inferredGoal: Keep Reference.type aligned with the set of concrete resource types in the target FHIR release.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Broaden the R6 base terminology to retain R4-only resource-type names as deprecated historical aliases, rather than relying only on converter guidance or ConceptMaps.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of aligning `Reference.type` with the concrete resource types in the target FHIR release is reasonable, and the binding remains extensible rather than becoming a direct required-code hard break. Ordinary ConceptMaps or converter rules are useful mitigations but are not base-design alternatives. The plausible base alternative is to include deprecated historical aliases, which would help many old type strings but at a real interoperability cost because `resource-types` would no longer mean only current R6 resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base terminology design could have retained R4-only resource-type names in the R6 terminology as deprecated or historical aliases. That would preserve more R4 `Reference.type` values for validators and generated enums, but it would be incomplete: the corresponding resource structures may be absent or remodeled in R6, and systems could misinterpret historical aliases as active R6 resource targets. Official ConceptMaps would still be helpful migration evidence, but they are conversion support rather than the counted base alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Historical aliases would reduce validator and enum churn, but they would blur the R6 resource inventory and would not restore removed resource definitions.

evidence.detail: R4 Reference.type has an extensible binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/resource-types`.
R6 Reference.type keeps an extensible binding to the same canonical value set.
R4 ValueSet/resource-types includes the complete `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types` code system.
R6 ValueSet/resource-types includes explicit concepts from `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types`.
Package code-list comparison found 20 R6-only resource-type codes and 41 R4-only codes.

examples.examplesMd: Because the binding is extensible, these fragments illustrate conformance and tooling risk rather than a guaranteed base JSON parse failure. `CatalogEntry` is in the R4 resource-type code system but not the R6 resource-types value set; `ActorDefinition` is in R6 but not R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `Reference.type` did not change structurally, but the meaning of its bound code universe did. R4 and R6 both point to `ValueSet/resource-types`, yet the versioned value set contents differ substantially. This is a classic runtime/codegen risk: generated enums, resolver dispatch, validation messages, and cross-version transforms often treat resource type names as a closed version-specific list even when the formal binding is extensible.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base FHIR validation should not treat this as a required-binding hard failure because `Reference.type` is `uri` with an extensible binding. Nevertheless, when a FHIR resource type applies, conformant systems are expected to use the version's value set, and stricter tools may reject or warn on removed codes. R6 codes such as `ActorDefinition` are not cleanly representable in R4 because R4 lacks both the code and the corresponding resource definition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate resource-type enums and resolver logic from the target FHIR package. During R4-to-R6 conversion, flag `Reference.type` values that are not in the R6 `resource-types` value set and map them only with an authoritative resource migration rule. During R6-to-R4 conversion, flag R6-only type values as lossy or unsupported unless the implementation has a cross-version extension or profile-specific mapping.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The value-set drift is largely unavoidable because `resource-types` reflects the release's resource inventory. The most backward-compatible support would be official alias/deprecation metadata and ConceptMaps for resource renames/removals. Without those, implementations must avoid assuming that identical value-set canonicals mean identical code content across FHIR releases.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should decide whether removed resource names have accepted R6 replacements, whether any should be mapped to new R6 resources, and whether local profiles intentionally allow historical resource-type names.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Reference.type remains a uri with an extensible binding to the same ValueSet/resource-types canonical, but the versioned value-set content changes materially between R4 and R6. This is not a simple required-binding hard failure in base validation, yet it can break generated resource-type enums, resolver dispatch, strict terminology checks, and cross-version transforms that assume the canonical value set has stable membership. The migration burden is real, but the value set is meant to track the resource inventory of the release, so retaining removed R4 resource names as ordinary R6 resource-type codes would create misleading semantics.
keyEvidence: R4 and R6 StructureDefinition-Reference keep Reference.type as uri 0..1 with extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/resource-types.
R4 ValueSet/resource-types includes the http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types code system; the R4 CodeSystem has 148 resource-type concepts.
R6 ValueSet/resource-types includes 127 explicit concepts from http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types.
Package comparison found 41 R4-only codes, such as Media, ChargeItem, and MedicationKnowledge, and 20 R6-only codes, such as ActorDefinition, DeviceAssociation, and SubscriptionTopic.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Normative Reference status raises the need to check for hard validation impact. The extensible binding and release-specific resource inventory temper the concern: this is mainly runtime/tooling and conversion work rather than an unavoidable base instance invalidation.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated enums, reference resolvers, validators configured stricter than extensible semantics, and R4/R6 converters may fail or need mapping when resource-type codes are removed, added, or moved to the fhir-types system.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could theoretically keep legacy R4 resource-type codes as inactive or deprecated concepts, but doing so in the base resource-types value set would imply that removed R4 resource definitions remain valid R6 reference targets. ConceptMaps, alias/deprecation metadata, and migration guidance are useful mitigations, but they are not a cleaner less-breaking base design that preserves the same release-inventory semantics.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report appropriately treats this as potential rather than definite hard instance break, with medium runtime/codegen and conversion risk. I also agree that there is no low-cost less-breaking base design that preserves the R6 goal.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The artifact id, canonical URL, name, kind, abstract flag, and type remain `Reference`. The baseDefinition changed from `Element` to `DataType`, but that is treated as an inherited/global datatype hierarchy issue and excluded from local findings.
No local Reference child elements were added, removed, renamed, split, or moved. R4 and R6 both define `reference`, `type`, `identifier`, and `display` in addition to inherited `id` and `extension`.
Local cardinalities are unchanged: each of `reference`, `type`, `identifier`, and `display` remains `0..1`; the root remains `0..*`.
Local element datatypes are unchanged: `Reference.reference` and `Reference.display` are `string`, `Reference.type` is `uri`, and `Reference.identifier` is `Identifier`.
The base `Reference` datatype itself does not declare targetProfiles. Target restrictions are supplied by resource/profile elements that use Reference and are out of scope for this datatype report.
No local Reference element has a fixed value, pattern, or default value in either R4 or R6.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex limit changes were found on Reference elements.
The root and local children are not modifiers in both versions.
`reference`, `type`, `identifier`, and `display` remain summary elements; inherited `id` and `extension` remain non-summary.
No local slicing was found on Reference-owned elements. The inherited `extension` slicing is a base Element/DataType concern and was not treated as a local finding.

No local JSON/XML property names, primitive representations, or choice-type serializations changed for Reference. The meaningful runtime risks are invariants and resource-type terminology, not wire-format shape.

Several comments and short descriptions were clarified, including `Reference.type` and `Reference.identifier`; the material semantic effects are captured in findings or notable changes. Separate ballot narrative pages were not reviewed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds guidance for additional identifiers via extension
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Reference.identifier` remains optional `0..1` and its datatype remains `Identifier`; the added R6 text is guidance, not a new cardinality or validation rule.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that used multiple logical identifiers in local extensions should review the referenced `additionalIdentifier` extension guidance for better R6 alignment.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 marks Reference with type characteristic has-target
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new StructureDefinition metadata extension documents that Reference has a target; it does not change instance element names, cardinalities, or local validation by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or model introspection tools that consume `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` may now classify Reference more explicitly as a target-bearing datatype.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 clarifies the RESTful relative reference pattern without the leading slash
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Reference.reference` remains optional `string` and the core semantics of relative, absolute, version-specific, and internal references remain the same.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation and tests should prefer the conventional `ResourceType/id` form when illustrating relative RESTful references.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 changes Reference's baseDefinition from `Element` to `DataType`. Per the inherited/base-artifact scope rule, superclass and generated hierarchy impacts should be assessed in the DataType/Element reports rather than duplicated here.

`Reference.type` depends on the version-specific `resource-types` value set. A terminology-focused follow-up should provide authoritative expansion evidence and mappings for R4-only and R6-only resource-type codes.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: R4/R6 resource inventory and rename/removal analysis
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Some `Reference.type` values differ because resource artifacts were added, removed, or renamed outside this datatype. Resource-level reports should own those identity and migration findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, Jira ticket, or ballot change rationale was available locally for Reference.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Reviewing official HL7 change notes or the generated diff page for Reference would improve confidence about intent and migration expectations.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The resource-type comparison used package compose/code-system content and did not call a terminology server for formal expansion or subsumption metadata.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A terminology-server expansion for both versions, plus any official ConceptMap between resource-type universes, would resolve code-list and mapping uncertainty.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The `ref-1` context analysis is based on the FHIRPath expressions in the StructureDefinitions; no executable R4/R6 validator was run against contained-resource examples.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Running both version validators on examples with root and contained-resource contexts would confirm the exact operational behavior for `reference="#"`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Generated narrative embedded in the StructureDefinitions was available, but separate published narrative pages and ballot discussion were not reviewed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Reviewing the R4 and R6 Reference specification pages would improve nuance for comments and examples, though the computable findings are already visible in the package artifacts.
